target_customer: Plaintiffs and businesses needing capital against lawsuits, government receivables or special situations; outside limited partners fund the investments
problem: Meritorious commercial claims and government receivables go unfunded because courts and agencies are slow, and underwriting cases is costly.
business_model: Investment fund manager with management fees and carry, deploying capital into legal assets

founders.name: Eva Shang
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch (Sept 2019) says she was 23 then, a Harvard dropout and Thiel Fellow; exact age at founding not stated.

founders.name: Christian Haigh
founders.background_notes: Named co-founder in TechCrunch 2019 and as General Partner on legalist.com; the YC page lists only Eva Shang.

technical_complexity.rationale: A data pipeline that scrapes court dockets to find cases was a moderate engineering task for two founders, but the hard part was legal underwriting, which humans still do.

defensibility.rationale: Proprietary sourcing data and an underwriting track record help, but capital and talent are available to larger funders; scale came from adding strategies.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Large funders such as Burford and Parabellum stayed focused on big cases and Legalist expanded into other legal asset strategies instead of competing head on, per Bloomberg Law coverage.

market_need_then: Litigation finance was a growing asset class with few funders for mid-sized claims. TechCrunch 2019 notes a growing number of funders; YC 2016 batch gave the founders the venture to apply their database to cases.

branding.brand_signature: Truffle sniffer, the nickname for its case sourcing algorithm
branding.community_and_virality: Press coverage centers on the young Harvard dropout founders, including a Wall Street Journal profile hosted on the company site and Bloomberg Law stories.

brand_strength.rationale: The name states the niche clearly and the founders' story drew press (WSJ, TechCrunch, Bloomberg Law), but the brand is about the founders and fund performance rather than a consumer-facing identity.

pivots.from: Software and database business built from court records
pivots.to: Litigation finance fund using that database to pick cases
pivots.why: An advisor recommended applying the database to litigation finance (Wikipedia summary of Eva Shang).

outcome_analysis: Legalist pivoted in 2016 from a database idea to a litigation finance fund, raised a $10.2M first fund, a $100M fund in 2019 and a $415M fourth fund in April 2026, and says it manages about $2B across strategies. Growth came from adding government receivables and special situations rather than fighting large funders. Risks include a public fee dispute with a former client in 2026 and case concentration; there is no exit or shutdown.
notes: Legalist is an investment manager, so its fund closes are not venture equity rounds and are listed here instead: first fund $10.2M, $100M fund announced 2019-09-17 (TechCrunch, Law.com), fourth fund $415M in April 2026 (Bloomberg Law; company site says Fund IV). AUM reports vary ($700M older, $1.5B 2025, $2.0B 2026). TechCrunch 2019 says Y Combinator owns 7% and VY Capital and Refactor Capital are equity holders; no amounts. The Thiel grant date is not stated in the source. Competitor list empty: Burford and Parabellum are named only in 2026 coverage, no source dated near 2016 was found. Name origin not found. Education and founders from TechCrunch 2019 and legalist.com General Partner list.
